reason: E1 shows that oxide layers on a Ni-based alloy at 600°C are mechanically unstable and delaminate, supporting the premise of wear-induced oxide disruption. However, E2 concerns a different refractory HEA processed by powder metallurgy and does not address oxide stability, corrosion, or synergistic wear-corrosion mechanisms. No evidence is cited for the corrosion acceleration, pit formation, or the specific eutectic HEA system, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: High-temperature oxide layers on HEAs can be mechanically unstable and delaminate under wear
Oxide removal exposes fresh metal to corrosion
Exposed metal corrodes rapidly, forming pits that act as stress concentrators
Pits accelerate wear, creating a synergistic degradation loop
The proposed mechanism applies to eutectic HEAs at 600°C in mildly acidic conditions
